Site changes

Here is every change I make to this site, with a picture of before and after. The newest is first.

Breed guides, clearer answers and easier returns

28 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.28b

A page for each breed.

Holland Lops and Netherland Dwarfs each have a guide, with purebreds and crosses kept separate. The breed names beside the filters, in Which rabbit? and on each rabbit’s page lead there. Long names keep their room on Which rabbit?.

The four questions stay together.

People ask is one clear group on a listing. The four answers still open over the same rabbit, and closing an answer returns to its button.

Allergy advice before a visit.

The answer says rabbits, hay and bedding can cause symptoms and recommends specialist advice if allergies or asthma are a concern. It links its sources and offers a video call or more photos.

The Christmas Eve reminder is shorter.

Christmas Eve · Free care until 24 Dec. The same promise fits in less space; it still appears only from 1 to 24 December for a rabbit ready to go home.

Return to the rabbit you opened.

Closing a listing returns keyboard focus to its rabbit, including payment rows in Safari. Rabbit links also open their own pages in a new tab; an ordinary tap still opens the listing here.

The litter filters show choices you can use.

An empty category no longer gets a filter. Buy and Reserve are named with the words on screen, and the News summary uses the most recent week of recorded updates.

Answers on the listing, and what this week looked like28 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.28a

Four questions people ask, answered on every listing.

Under a rabbit’s listing, four small buttons: How big will it get? Litter box? Cats or dogs? How long do they live? A tap opens the answer from Things people ask right over the listing, and closing it leaves you on the same rabbit.

How many were reserved this week, beside how many went home.

Next to “22 gone home”, a line counts the rabbits reserved in the last seven days, from the record, so it rises and falls by itself. It shows from two up and never names a rabbit or a buyer.

A coming litter says what the same parents’ last ones did.

When a coming litter’s parents have had babies here before, one line under the ready day says what happened to their last ones, worked out from the record: “Their last six all went home. Each was reserved within a day of going on sale, at $400 to $450.” Every pair gets it, whatever the record says, and a first litter gets none.

In December, every listing repeats the Christmas Eve promise.

From 1 to 24 December, under “Ready to go home now”, a listing says: “Home on Christmas Eve? I keep it here until 24 Dec, at no extra cost.” It is the promise already in the Christmas row, nothing new, and it leaves on its own on 25 December.

Two new answers: allergies, and a 4-H project.

Under “Is it right for you?”: “Allergic, or not sure?” says to hold one first on a free visit. “Starting a 4-H rabbit project?” says only purebreds can be shown at the Pima County Fair, the 2027 fair runs 15 to 25 April, and the rabbit must be yours by 1 April, from the county’s own rabbit rules. The front page’s search title now reads “Arizona Rabbits · Bunnies for sale in Tucson”, each rabbit in the list for search engines points to its own page, and the pedigree PDFs stay out of search results. Each rabbit’s name after the address also opens its page: arizonarabbits.com/sprinkles.

Each rabbit’s own family27 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.27l

Parents links follow each rabbit.

In a pair, each rabbit’s breed bar opens that rabbit’s own family. Editing either rabbit and going back keeps both selections.

Three generations recorded, explained.

The pedigree outline means both parents, four grandparents and eight great-grandparents are named. The information beside it explains that coverage; other identifying details can still be missing.

Tajima’s full video, with original sound.

The latest litter clip preserves the full original picture, including the faces near the end, and restores its original sound. English and Spanish captions load correctly. Recent litter photographs keep their framing and use the same finish.

Pair controls stay clear.

The pair toolbar has a solid background while you scroll. Portraits and names fit narrow landscape screens, and each rabbit keeps its own edit control.

A sold rabbit’s link says Sold27 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.27k

A shared link to a rabbit that went home now says Sold.

The label on the picture reads Sold, and the preview’s title says “Mocha was sold and went home.” Reserved rabbits keep their Reserved label, and rabbits still for sale keep a plain picture.

A shared link shows when a rabbit is spoken for27 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.27j

A link to a rabbit you can no longer buy now says so in its preview.

When a rabbit’s link is sent in a text or a post, its picture carries a small brick label, Reserved, Gone home or Stays with us, and the preview’s title says the same: “Snickerdoodle is reserved.” A rabbit still for sale keeps its plain picture. Snickerdoodle and Mochi were reserved today; the price checks and the pages were read back on the live site.

Waiting counts: under three, the total only27 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.27i

Under three of a litter’s own, only the total is shown.

When fewer than three people asked for a litter itself, the litter now gives only the whole number: “6 people are waiting on the litter born 5 November.” The split into “follow every litter” and “asked for this one” shows once a litter has three of its own. In Spanish, the plain form of the line is now fully in Spanish too; before, only the litter’s name was translated.

Waiting counts, told apart27 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.27h

The people waiting are counted once, and told apart.

Each coming litter showed everyone who will hear about it, so the same people on the every-litter list were counted on every card: 6, 5 and 5 for six people in all. Now the shelf says once, “5 people get an alert for every new litter”. A card shows its own number only when at least three people asked for that litter itself. Opened, a litter still gives the whole number and what it is made of: “6 people are waiting on the litter born 5 November: 5 follow every litter, and 1 asked for this one.”

Each rabbit’s own page, more useful27 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.27g

A rabbit’s own page has its photos and the two buttons.

Under the photo, the rabbit’s other photos and its clip are small squares, one tap each. In place of one long button there are the site’s two, “Reserve · $50” and “Buy” with today’s price, and each opens the listing with the request sheet ready. A row below leads to the full listing.

A rabbit that went home shows who is still here.

The page of a rabbit that went home now shows its littermates still for sale, each with its photo, name and price. If none is left, it shows others for sale of the same breed.

Every rabbit that went home, by month27 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.27f

See every rabbit that went home, by month.

Under the breed buttons, “22 gone home” shows every rabbit that has gone home from here, in place of the rabbits for sale. The newest month comes first, and each month shows its rabbits’ photos, grouped by litter. List opens that month as a plain list with small photos and the day each one went home. Each photo opens that rabbit’s record. The count grows by itself.

More rabbits on the screen27 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.27e

On a computer, four rabbits across, each card whole.

The rabbits used to start two across on every screen, so on a computer twelve rabbits took six rows. Now the grid starts at what fits: two on a phone, three on a tablet, four on a computer, and from a tablet’s width up every card keeps its breed, age and both buttons. The Columns choice is still there, and a choice you make is remembered.

On a phone, the first two rabbits show whole.

After “See 12 rabbits”, one line stays under the heading, “The price you see is the whole price.”, with a More button for the rest. The count is still said by the All button, and Columns now sits in the Aa panel with Text size. So the first two cards, with their Reserve buttons, fit on the first screen.

Litters counted fairly, waiting counts, and the free switch27 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.27d

The Litters page counts new litters fairly.

Its first line said how many rabbits found homes within four weeks of being listed, while two litters listed this month had not had their four weeks yet. Until they have, it says how many already have homes, and the rabbits still inside their four weeks are “ready now”, with a link to them.

Each coming litter shows how many people are waiting.

On the photo of each litter on the way, above the count of babies, a small pill with an icon says how many people are on its list, from three up. It is a number only, never a name, and it comes from the same list as the sign-up box.

The free first switch is said where littermates are chosen.

On the request sheet of a rabbit with littermates for sale, one line says: reserve one, and your first switch to another rabbit is free, one per person. The answer about the deposit and the Terms now say the same: one free switch per person, even if you take two.

The menu’s icon on the rabbits, and Home on litter photos27 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.27c

The rabbits’ section carries the menu’s icon.

On a phone, each section the menu names has a small label above its heading, with the menu’s own icon. “Meet the rabbits” was the only one without. It now says “Available” with the price tag, the same word and icon as the menu.

Litter photos say where they were taken: at home.

A litter photo’s line now ends with a pin and “Home”, beside how old the babies were that day. It is on the litter cards on the front page and in the photo viewer on the Litters page.

A sale’s last day, and home by Christmas27 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.27b

A sale’s last day is under the price.

A listing under a dated sale now says the sale’s name and its last day right under the price, and the request sheet says the same under the rabbit’s name. Before, the listing showed only the two prices, and the reason and the day were inside “What you pay for”. The words are worked out from the sale’s own dates, so they leave by themselves when the sale ends. Each rabbit’s own page says the same words.

A sale shows on the first screen while it runs.

While a dated sale is running, the rows on the first screen begin with it: its name, its last day, how many rabbits are under it and what they cost. Opened, the row shows those rabbits, each one a link to its listing. Before, the sale showed only on its own cards, three and a half screens down. The row is written from the records and leaves by itself when the sale is over.

“Home by Christmas” is answered first.

The Christmas row now begins with two answers. The first says which rabbits can be home by Christmas: the ones ready now, and the litters whose ready day comes before it, worked out from the records. The second says that a reserved rabbit can stay here until 24 December at no extra cost. The five reminders that were already there stay.

One price on every page27 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.27a

A rabbit’s own page now shows the same price as its listing.

A price that changes by the clock, like this weekend’s Thanksgiving price, used to reach only the listing. Each rabbit’s own page kept the price from the day the site was last built, $30 more for six rabbits. Every page now reads the same record at the moment you open it.

Which rabbit lists only the rabbits you can still get.

Pepper and Coconut were reserved on 25 November and were still shown for sale here, and six prices were the old ones. The lists, the counts and the price ranges now follow the records, so a reserved rabbit leaves this page as soon as it is marked reserved.

The price answer gives the range, and it is always today’s.

“Why do they cost what they cost?” used to name fourteen rabbits with their prices, written when the site was last built. It now says what the prices run from and to, worked out from the records as you read it. Each rabbit’s own price is on its listing.

S'Morri and Root Beer’s litter26 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.26j

S'Morri and Root Beer’s litter: two Holland Lops, born 20 November.

They are with the litters coming soon on the front page, with a photo at six days old, and they have their own page on Litters. They are projected ready on Thursday 17 December.

Two rabbits together, clearer to the last step26 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.26i

Under two rabbits’ photos, everything follows their order.

On the page for two, the breed bars could list the rabbits in the opposite order from their photos. The names, the bars and the prices now follow the photos, left and then right.

The military and first responder discount shows on each rabbit.

Turn the switch on and a 5% mark now sits under each rabbit with its new price, and the price for the two at the top changes with it.

The payment plan is the last question, at its real price.

The request sheet used to offer a plan beside Reserve and Buy. It now asks last, “How will you pay the rest?”, and shows what a plan costs: full price, within a month and a half per rabbit. For two, one line replaces the “Taking two?” box.

Shorter cards, parents’ faces, a pedigree in rows26 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.26h

Each tile now holds its drawing, its name and its count on a single line, so the first rabbits start higher on the screen.

A rabbit’s card is about a fifth shorter on a phone.

Three lines that every card said in the same words are trimmed, so Reserve and Buy come sooner. Nothing about the rabbit itself was taken out.

A small photo of each parent sits beside its name.

Where a listing names the mother and the father, each name now has that parent’s face next to it.

The pedigree reads as rows you can tap.

The two narrow parent cards and their small buttons are now full-width rows, the father and then the mother, each opening that rabbit’s page. A line under each says what is on record about its family.

A listing’s photo, with more light and more to say26 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.26g

The space beside and under the photo now takes its colour from the photo itself, softened and dimmed, and a clip does the same while it plays. The date line is slimmer.

Each photo says how long ago it was taken, and where.

Under a listing’s photo you now read how many days ago it was taken, then the date, then the place when I have recorded it.

Turn your phone and the photo fills the screen from top to bottom.

In the enlarged view, a phone on its side now gives the full height of the screen to the photo. The name, the arrows and the date sit over it and fade until you tap.

Where I am26 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.26f

My address is on the site.

The footer, the Contact section and the answer about visits now name The Place at Creekside and its street address, with a link to the map. I send the apartment number once your visit is booked.

Snapchat is no longer one of the ways to reach me.

A jump lands on its heading and lights what you came for.

The breed chips over the coming litters fit a phone.

The Home button no longer sits on the breed tiles.

A link that opens another page now says so.

A litter opens right where you are.

A tap on a litter on the front page used to send you off to the Litters page. Its sheet now opens over the page you are on, and closing it leaves you exactly where you were.

Delivery and Which rabbit look like the rest of the site.

Both pages now carry the same header as every other page, with the row of section links under it, and both follow dark mode with their own switch.

Text size, and even spacing in the About21 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.21d

You can now make the text smaller or larger.

Tap “Aa” and pick Smaller, Standard or Larger. The whole page changes together and keeps its layout, and your choice stays on your device. On a phone, “Aa” is the third circle on the photo, and it is at the foot of the page too. On a computer, it is in the top bar where the moon was, with the dark mode switch inside it.

The About now has clear, even spacing.

Each block has the same space before the next, the heading and the photo have more room around them, and no text wraps under the photo. The spacing grows and shrinks with the text size. On narrower screens it reads in one column; on wider ones the photo sits beside the introduction.

The About, in short blocks21 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.21c

The About now opens with the winning lines, in short blocks.

The line under the name now reads “I pay top dollar for winning lines from all across the world.” Then each block opens with a bold line: the purebreds and their pedigrees, how each line is bred to get better, how every baby is handled, and what you are paying for. Where the money goes, every litter’s record and what comes next, chinchillas and then Persian cats, open under “Where the money goes, and more”.

A familiar dot, a mix that lines up, sheets that stay put21 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.21b

The dot for rabbits you have not seen yet is the familiar red one.

Where the row of rabbits slides sideways, the dot on its arrow is now the small red dot phones use for something new, sitting on the arrow’s corner instead of beside it, and the number beside the arrow, how many rabbits are that way, stays white. The dot still means only that some of them are new to you, and it still goes once you have seen them all.

In a cross’s mix, each breed sits under its own colour.

The key under a cross’s bar now lines up with the bar: each breed’s share and name begin exactly where its colour begins, so none hangs on a line of its own or sits under the wrong colour. On the narrowest phones, where three breeds cannot stand side by side, each takes a line of its own with its colour’s dot, and a name is never broken. Parents is on its own line at the right.

A sheet stays put while you read it, and its X stays in reach.

A litter’s sheet, the closer look, the alerts sheet and the answers now hold the page behind them still, as a rabbit’s listing does, so a finger or the mouse wheel on the dark area moves nothing and the sheet no longer slides with your phone’s bars. The X stays at the top corner while you scroll through the sheet, so you can close it from anywhere without scrolling back up; as the words reach it, a bar with the sheet’s title fades in behind it, as on a rabbit’s listing, so they never run under it. Closing it leaves the page where it was.

Snow in every scene, every line whole21 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.21a

Snow in both little Christmas scenes, falling as it does in the village.

The houses above “The rabbits behind every litter” and the sled above “What you take home” now snow the whole time they are on your screen, like the village at the foot of every page, and the sled’s luminarias flicker gently. The village’s own snow no longer jumps at the end of each loop, and three thin straight lines along its edges are gone. Pause in the village holds every flake still, and nothing moves for visitors who ask for less motion.

Every line whole: a litter’s parents and the waitlist.

Where a parent’s ear number is too long for its line, the papers now take two lines, the ear number and then the pedigree, in both parents’ cards, instead of being cut short, and the two cards’ papers begin level. On the waitlist, each litter’s breed and “Purebred” or “Cross” stay on one line on any phone or computer from 360 pixels wide, so no word is left alone.

Tajima and Maximo’s first litter20 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.20l

Tajima and Maximo’s first litter: four born on 19 November.

All four were healthy the day after. Their page has Tajima in her nest box, the nest, both parents and the day they should be ready. They are with the litters coming soon on the front page, and under Netherland Dwarf in Which rabbit fits your home.

The rabbits you have not seen yet20 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.20k

A dot on the rabbits’ row while there are rabbits you have not seen.

Where the row of rabbits slides sideways, a small dot sits on its arrow while there are rabbits you have not seen yet, and when the last one comes into view the dot pops away. Your phone or computer remembers who you have seen, so the dot comes back only for a new rabbit. The arrow forward is a little bigger than the arrow back; the arrows spring back a touch when you let go, and the arrows that open a part turn with a little give.

Site version 2026.11.20j

Which rabbit fits your home?20 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.20i

Which rabbit fits your home? A page that helps you choose.

Holland Lops, Netherland Dwarfs and my crosses side by side, with my own prices. The answer to “How big will it get?” now ends with a link to it.

Site version 2026.11.20h

A page that breaks tells me where.

If one of the site’s scripts fails on your screen, the visit count now notes where in the code it happened, a file and a line, nothing else, so I can fix it. The terms say so in a new paragraph.

Delivery across Arizona, on one page20 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.20g

Christmas Eve in Tucson15 November 2026

Site version 2026.11.15e

Christmas Eve in a Tucson bunny village, drawn as one scene.

The scene at the foot of every page is drawn again as one illustration, like an old printed Christmas card: an adobe casita in a little village of bunny homes, with luminarias and a bunny in every lit window, one of them hanging an ornament on the tree; in the yard a bunny in a red scarf builds a snow bunny with a carrot nose; our rabbit in his Santa hat drives a sled of presents past a saguaro in lights, under the Catalinas and one star. On a phone it is a tall picture: the village stands together on the hill behind the casita, a street of three bunny homes with a smaller one beside it, then the village tree under the Christmas star, where a bunny on a ladder sets the star on its top, and one more home where another bunny strings lights along the roof, with a path of luminarias from the sled up to its door. On a computer the same village gathers around the casita and the sled. It moves gently only while it is on screen; Pause stops it, and it stays still for anyone who has turned motion off. The string of lights along the top of every page is redrawn to match: old painted-glass bulbs in no fixed order.

The scene melts into the page above and below.

The page now comes down into the sky on a frosted wave instead of a straight line. Under the snow, the ground is cut away like a cross section: dark soil in the dim look and deep snow in the light one, with Christmas goodies buried in it, an ornament, a candy cane, a gingerbread rabbit, a present. The list of rabbits ready before Christmas and the holiday greeting stand in it.

The list under the scene says what it is.

The button under the Christmas scene said “Open the presents”. It now says what it opens, “Ready before Christmas”, and over the rabbits’ faces is the line from the foot of every page: “A rabbit lives eight to twelve years. I’m here for all of them.” A tap on the sled’s presents lifts the lid on hay, a present for the bunnies.

The site's private count can tell a person's visit from an automated one.
